text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — acceptance checklist for the Optimize toolkit pilot surfaced a couple of customer edge cases we should nail down. One finance customer wants per-route eval-trigger thresholds + automatic rollback on major regressions. :thinking_face:
Devin: Can you paste the exact ask? Is this different from the eval-sentry behavior we sketched? https://go/redwood/docs/eval-sentry does mention alerts but not auto-rollbacks.
Maya: They want alerts scoped to prompt set + model variant, with severity mapping: minor -> notify, major -> automatic rollback to a pinned model version, and an audit log entry showing metric diffs.
Sarah: For MVP we planned notify-only. Auto-rollback touches safety/ops — needs runbooks and guardrails. That feels like a blocker if we try to include it now.
Liam: Another edge-case: an on-prem customer expects quantization profiles validated inside their environment. So not just recommending int8, but shipping a profile artifact + verification tests they can run locally.
Devin: That implies a portable profile format + small test harness. If we scope that in, it's an integration effort with Private/Dedicated which might push the pilot timeline.
Maya: Proposal for pilot acceptance gates: (A) eval-trigger alerts: per-prompt-set notify + manual rollback (no auto rollback), (B) batching/caching recommendations with a small sample-sim run and suggested config YAML, (C) quantization recommendations + hosted-model quant profiles (doc + example artifacts) only. Defer on-prem quant validation to Dedicated/Private phase.
Sarah: +1. We should explicitly call out "deferred for Private/Dedicated" in the acceptance checklist so Sales & SEs don't overpromise.
Liam: As a compromise, can we ship an "exportable profile" artifact and an unsupported runner script customers can use on-prem? Not validated by Redwood, just a convenience.
Devin: That sounds reasonable as a stop-gap. Add clear "unsupported" label and no SLAs.
Maya: Agreed. Minimal deliverables we should require for pilot: 1) per-prompt-set eval alerting (notify), 2) rollback docs + manual rollback flow, 3) batching/caching recommendation engine + sample sim results, 4) hosted quant profiles + docs, 5) export artifact + runner script for on-prem (unsupported).
Sarah: I'll update release notes and FAQs to call out the unsupported runner and the deferred validation scope.
Liam: I'll draft the export runner README and a tiny usage snippet:
```bash
# run exported quant profile verifier (unsupported)
python quant_profile_runner.py --profile /tmp/profile.pb --model-path /mnt/model --input-corpus ./sample_prompts.json
```
Devin: Action items: Maya update acceptance checklist and open the pilot gating PR, Sarah update comms and sales FAQ, Liam create the runner README + sample artifact, Devin to add the eval-alert severity mapping spec to the repo. Target: 1 week.
Maya: Filing the checklist PR now and linking tasks in the release board. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: release-bot added checklist item to board #optimize-pilot (card 4521)
QA-bot: QA reminder: include a smoke eval run against customer prompt sets before we mark pilot as accepted
Maya: Noted — I'll attach the customer prompt set sample to the checklist (sanitized) and tag QA.
Devin: Fine-grain follow-up: we should also add an item to capture metric thresholds and the diff calculation method (absolute vs relative). I'll sketch a tiny RFC and link it in the PR.
Maya: Great. Closing thread for now; will reopen if the customer pushes for auto-rollback.
